With the progressive development of trailer industry in India, it has been felt necessary to evolve code which would lay down standards to assess suitability of trailer in its intended role. In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`.

3 TERMINOLOGY 3.1 For the purpose of this standard, the terms and definitions given in IS 7774 ( Parts 1 and 2 ) : 1975 and along with the following shall apply. 3.1 .l Articulation Height for Single Axle It is the maximum lift of wheels on one end of the axle to the other end of the same tilted axle without affecting the ease of operation/functions of the various components/controls. 3.1.2 Articulation Height for Multi Axle It is the maximum height to which any two adjacent diagonally opposite wheels of an axle group of any trailer be subjected to lift without affecting the ease of operation/functions of various components/controls. 3.1.3 Near Side Near side of a tractor-trailer combination is the side which is nearer to the platform kerb or pavement where a tractor-trailer combination on parked for short periods usually zghways in the direction of move. The near side is the one towards the left of the driver when he is in the driving seat. 3.1.4 Offside is the side opposite to the

It is the brake for retarding, stopping controlling the tractor-trailer combination the combination is in motion. 3.1.10 Braking Distance

It is the distance travelled between the point of retardation by the brakes on a level ground and the point at which the trailer comes to rest. 3.1.11 Parking Brake

Parking brake is used for parking or holding the trailer or the tractor-trailer combination in unladen/laden condition either on a level ground or on a specified gradient. 3.1.12 Standard Performance Trials

A set of standard trials which will indicate the characteristics of the required performance tractor-trailer combination but will not include reliability and wear and tear properties. 3.1.13 Cross Country

Off side of a trailer near aide.

It is defined as a natural/virgin terrain other than metal roads and may comprise bullock cart or animal tracks, slushy or sandy terrains such as river bed cross and level or undulated ' boulder sections or hilly terrain with gradients. I

4 PERFORMANCE

TESTS Tests

4.1 General Performance 4.1.1 Initial Examination

Any new trailer on receipt from the firm shall be inspected to ascertain whether the tractortrailer combination is in conformity with the specifications and drawings of the approved prototype supplied by the makers. 4.1.2 Loading and Weighing The sample trailer shall be weighed in laden and unladen conditions to check axle load distributions. In laden condition, the trailers shall be loaded with the specified load and locations as per the specification. 4.1.3 Road Test on Selected Track on Public Road
4.1.3.1

The towing vehicle with the trailer in combination shall be driven in unladen/laden condition at specified restricted speed and maximum controllable speed. 4.1.3.4 General performance this test shall be recorded. 4.1.4 Articulation Test
4.1.4.1 The test shall be conducted levelled hard ground.

of the trailer

during

on a plain

4.1.4.2 The test shall be conducted in the fully laden condition of the trailer with specified tyre pressure. 4.1.4.3 Articulation height of each of the consecutive pairs of wheels shall be measured. 4.1.4.4 Observations regarding the fouling points, if any, shall be recorded. 2

A suitable test track consisting of different types of road surfaces like tar, tarmac and gravel, representing the general public road/high way conditions shall be selected for this test.

4.2.1.1 The lest track selected for this test shall be of rough, uneven boulder and hilly terrain. 4.2.1.2 It is preferable if the track crossing of river beds and slushy terrain be of at least 15 km run. 4.2.1.3 General performance be recorded durrng thrs test. 4.2.2 Endurance Trials of the includes and shall shall

4.1.6.2 Marking can be made on the ground, while the tractor-trailer combination is moved in the lowest possible speed at different types of drive, either by means of spray water or by means of a pointer. 4.1.6.3 Both minimum outer inner circle shall be checked. and corresponding

4.1.6.4 Minimum outer tractor-trailer combination clearance circle and the corresponding inner tractor-trailer combination clearance circle shall be checked. 4.1.7 Brake Performance Tests in

4.2.2.1 After a trailer has been tested for assessment of its performance under various tests/trials as expiained above, it may be subjected to endurance trials. The aim of these trials is to observe the sturdiness and capability of the trailers, its components assemblies and parts and to record any defects, maintenance difficulties etc, that would be normally experienced during prolonged service under actual operating conditions and which could not be brought out during standard performance trials. 4.2.2.2 The trailer, which is selected for endurance trials shall be kept under observation during the trial period. The required kilometerage for completion of endurance trials shall depend opon the type of trailer and its intended role. During endurance trials, the trailers shall be used in their intended role without any misuse or abuse of any part or any assembly/component. The trailer shall be run in highway/cross country/kacha roads as recommended for the trailer use. 4.2.2.3 After completion of endurance trials, various major assemblies/sub-assemblies shall be stripped open to check the condition of various components and wear rates of various moving parts.

The brake performance shall be checked accordance with IS 11852 ( Part 3 ) : 1987. 4.1.8 Lighting Equipment Tests

All the electrical fittings like tractor-trailer couplers, brake lamps, indicator lamps, tail lamps, etc, shall be checked during day as well as night for intended functions.
